Keypad button inventory

Satisfies AC10, AC12

Exactly 17 buttons: 0–9, decimal point, +, −, ×, ÷, C, =. No %, sign-toggle (±), or memory keys (M+/M−/MR) — deferred pending team confirmation of the basic button set, per the work item's stated scope. Every key renders at least 58px tall, comfortably above the 44×44px minimum touch target.

Empty display

AC1 — nothing typed yet

Both lines render blank until the first key is tapped.

Typing: expression + live result

AC1, AC2
12+8×3
36

Every tapped character appears on the expression line; the result line evaluates live using × before + (8×3=24, 12+24=36).

Cleared

AC3 — after tapping C

Identical to the empty state — C always resets fully, even mid-error.

Finalized result

AC4 — after tapping =
12+8×3
36

The result line switches from a muted live preview to a bold, finalized answer.

Expression font shrinking

AC5 — exceeds display width
1234+5678−910×11
6012

As the expression grows past the display's width, its font steps down progressively (two steps shown here) before reaching the minimum size.

Minimum size + scrolled

AC6, AC7
…1112÷13+9876−54×210
−3581.9

At minimum font size the line clips so the most-recently typed character stays at the right edge; tapping another key still appends to the expression.

Overflow

Results too large to display reliably show "Overflow" instead of a truncated or scientific-notation number.

Syntax Error

12+

An incomplete expression closed with "=" is a syntax error, not a silently-ignored tap.

Domain Error (illustrative)

AC8 — not reachable with this story's keypad
√(−9)
⚠ Domain Error

Shown for completeness only — a domain error needs a scientific function (e.g. √ of a negative number), which is out of scope for this story's basic button set.

Error recovery

AC9 — edit continues after an error

⚠ Divide by Zero

↓ tap "5" to edit the expression

5÷05

The moment the expression changes, the normal result line comes back — no separate "dismiss" step needed.

Decimal point rule

AC11
3.14
3.14

Tapping "." again here is ignored — this number segment already has one decimal point. Starting a new segment after an operator allows one new decimal point.

Screen-reader live region

Satisfies AC13

A visually-hidden aria-live="polite" region mirrors every expression, result, and error change as it happens, so a screen reader announces each update without the user needing to navigate to the display manually.
